newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN rights body urges Iran to halt violence.
newsitem.headline: UN rights body urges Iran to halt violence.

text.p: The U.N. Human Rights Commission on Tuesday passed a resolution urging Iran to "refrain from violence against members of the Iranian opposition living abroad" and extending the mandate of its investigator for the country.
The 53-member forum also expressed concern about continuing violations of human rights, especially the "large number of executions", and cases of torture, including amputation.
The resolution called on the government to provide "satisfactory written assurances that it does not support or incite threats to the life of (British writer Salman) Rushdie".

A major Iranian exile group, the Paris-based National Council of Reistance (NCR), issued a statement praising the vote as "another irrefutable document underlining the need to reject the mullahs' regime from the international community".
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 26 countries in favour, seven against with 19 abstentions and one delegation absent for the vote at the annual session which ends on Friday.

The resolution extended by one year the mandate of U.N. special rapporteur for Iran, Canadian jurist Maurice Copithorne. In his annual speech to the Commission two weeks ago, he implicitly rebuked Iran for maintaining a high rate of death sentences, for persecution of religious dissidents, for killings of dissenters abroad and for new pressures on the press.
